newsitem.title: USA: First Merchants Acceptance shares fall.
newsitem.headline: First Merchants Acceptance shares fall.

text.p: First Merchants Acceptance Corp shares fell sharply Thursday, a day after the used auto financing company said it discovered irregularities in its financial records and dismissed its chief executive officer and three other employees.
First Merchants shares were down three at 3-5/8 Thursday.

Derfield, Illinois-based First Merchants also said its first quarter results would be delayed and it expected to report a loss of $1.60 to $2 a share for the quarter. First Merchants had previously said it expected a quarter near breakeven.

The company also said the irregularities caused the company to be out of compliance with certain covenants under its financiang agreements, though all payments have been made on a timely basis and the company is in discussions with its lenders.

Financing is key to companies like First Merchants, which borrow money to purchase auto loans from auto dealers, then make money on the spread between the interest rates of what they borrow and what they loan.

The announcement late Wednesday was reminiscent of problems at Mercury Finance Co, another subprime auto lender, which in January said it had to restate its earnings over the last four years, cutting profits by about $90 million, because of what it said were accounting descrepencies.
"The terminology that they used in saying what was going on with the company is similar," Kevin Spinner, analyst at Keefe Bruyette & Woods Inc said.
First Merchants said the irregularities involved unauthorized entries made in the company's financial records. The company did not return repeated telephone calls seeking elaboration.

Spinner said the problems could be related to how the company was carrying some loans on its books and others who follow the industry said the Mercury case has forced other subprime auto lenders to become more conservative with their financial data.
"I don't think the CEO is going in with a pencil and making up numbers," Spinner said.
